title: Why the Mecca Agreement Might Fail
author: Natiq Malikzada
text:
Credit: Facebook / Shehbaz Sharif
On August 7, 2026, Turkiye’s Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, Saudi Arabia’s Mohammed bin Salman, and Pakistan’s Shehbaz Sharif jointly signed the Mecca  Joint Defense Agreement, which commits their countries to collective defense and expands defense cooperation. It builds on the Saudi-Pakistani Strategic Mutual Defense Agreement of September 2025. On August 31, their foreign ministers, defense ministers, and military chiefs met in Istanbul, announcing a secretariat in Saudi Arabia, initially headed by a Pakistani secretary general, alongside cooperation in military technology and production.The most important question about the Mecca agreement is whose war they are prepared to fight. Although the text of the agreement is not publicly available yet, according to a Pakistan Foreign Ministry statement, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan have agreed that an armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all. However, with a look at their conflicting interests, one can easily predict that they will struggle to agree on what should happen next.[...]
